item.title: Germany votes to let military intercept drones
item.description:
Germany's parliament on Thursday voted to expand the military's authority to intercept or shoot down drones, responding to a surge in unidentified aerial activity that officials have linked to Russia's hybrid warfare campaign against Europe.

The Bundestag approved an amendment to the country's air security law with support from the governing conservatives, the Social Democrats, and the far-right Alternative for Germany opposition, according to Reuters. The legislation marks the culmination of months of political urgency over rogue drones spotted near airports, military bases, and critical infrastructure across the country.

item.title: Pakistan declares 'open war' on Afghanistan after deadly border clashes
item.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan plunged into their most dangerous military confrontation in years as the Taliban launched a large-scale ground offensive against Pakistani positions along the disputed Durand Line on Thursday evening, prompting Pakistani airstrikes on Kabul, Kandahar, and Paktia province hours later. Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif declared "open war" against Afghanistan on Friday, posting on X: "Our patience has reached its limit. Now it is open war between us and you."

The rapidly escalating conflict, unfolding during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan, has shattered a fragile ceasefire brokered by Qatar last October and drawn the nuclear-armed neighbors into their most direct military engagement since the Taliban seized power in 2021.

item.title: Nintendo plans $1.9B share sale as banks unwind stakes
item.description:
Nintendo is preparing for a roughly $1.9 billion share sale as major lenders including MUFG Bank and the Bank of Kyoto move to offload their strategic stakes in the "Super Mario" maker, Reuters first reported on Thursday, citing three people familiar with the matter.

The disposal is expected to amount to about 300 billion yen, and a decision could come as early as Friday. The Kyoto-based gaming company is also planning a share buyback to help absorb the supply, the sources said. Nintendo did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Nvidia drops sharply despite record earnings as Block cuts half its staff
item.description:
Nvidia erased roughly $260 billion in market value on Thursday despite delivering another blockbuster quarter, dragging the Nasdaq Composite to its sharpest decline in weeks and unsettling global investors already on edge over the durability of the AI boom. Separately, fintech firm Block announced it would eliminate more than 4,000 jobs — nearly half its workforce — in what its co-founder Jack Dorsey called a structural shift driven by artificial intelligence.

The two developments, arriving on the same trading day, underscored a growing tension in markets: companies at the center of the AI revolution are posting record results, yet investors are demanding ever more proof that the spending frenzy will translate into lasting profits.

item.title: Asian shares fall as Nvidia slump and Pakistan-Afghanistan war rattle markets
item.description: Asian markets fell on Friday as concerns over technology company valuations and a string of geopolitical flashpoints drove investors toward safe-haven assets, extending the cautious tone set by Wall Street's overnight decline. The yen and U.S. Treasuries strengthened, while gold held steady near elevated levels.

item.title: ESA releases first image of comet 3I/ATLAS from its Jupiter-bound spacecraft
item.description: Eight months after its discovery electrified astronomers worldwide, interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS is speeding away from the inner solar system, leaving behind a trail of scientific revelations about the chemistry of deep space. The ancient visitor — only the third object ever confirmed to have arrived from beyond our solar system — is now headed toward a close pass of Jupiter next month before vanishing into the interstellar void forever.

item.title: Oil slides as U.S. and Iran extend nuclear talks
item.description: Gold prices held firm near recent highs on Friday while oil slipped toward a weekly loss after the United States and Iran wrapped up their third round of indirect nuclear negotiations in Geneva without a deal but with a commitment to keep talking. The extension of diplomacy eased fears of an imminent military confrontation that could disrupt Middle Eastern energy supplies, pulling crude lower even as bullion remained supported by broader safe-haven demand.

item.title: Canada's Carney arrives in India to reset ties after diplomatic crisis
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in Mumbai on Friday, launching a four-day visit to India that marks his first official trip to the country since taking office and signals a diplomatic reset after years of strained ties between Ottawa and New Delhi.

item.title: Chinese scientists achieve 700 Wh/kg lithium battery breakthrough
item.description:
A team of Chinese researchers has developed a novel lithium battery electrolyte system that achieves an energy density of 700 watt-hours per kilogram at room temperature — more than double the capacity of the best commercially available lithium-ion batteries. The findings, published February 25 in Nature, represent a potential leap forward for electric vehicles, aerospace, and cold-weather energy storage.

The research was led by Professor Zhao Qing from the College of Chemistry at Nankai University, Academician Chen Jun, the university's executive vice president, and Researcher Li Yong from the Shanghai Institute of Space Power-Sources. Their approach replaces the conventional carbonate ester solvents used in commercial lithium battery electrolytes with a series of fluorinated hydrocarbon solvent molecules, establishing a lithium-fluorine coordination system in place of the traditional lithium-oxygen mechanism.

item.title: Zelenskyy says he's ready to meet Putin for peace talks
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he is ready to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin face-to-face to resolve the most difficult issues standing in the way of peace, while warning that surrendering Ukrainian-held fortress cities in the east remains a firm red line.

In a wide-ranging interview with Sky News published on February 27, Zelenskyy said there is a closing window to end the war — one tied to American domestic politics. "Now I think that we have a chance," he told correspondent Alex Rossi. "If it will be possible to achieve a peace, we will have, now we have this window" — between now and the U.S. midterm elections in November.

item.title: Astronomers reveal trio of rare cosmic finds in single week
item.description: In a burst of discoveries announced over the past week, astronomers using some of the world's most advanced telescopes have revealed three rare and violent cosmic phenomena: the first image of a young Sun-like star inflating a protective bubble in space, possible evidence of an elusive black hole shredding a white dwarf, and the fading radio echo of a powerful explosion whose original blast went unseen.

item.title: Chinese scientists set world records for kesterite, polymer solar cells
item.description:
Researchers in China have announced back-to-back breakthroughs in solar cell technology, setting world records for both kesterite and polymer photovoltaic devices in findings published this week.

The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) reported that its Qingdao Institute of Bioenergy and Bioprocess Technology fabricated a kesterite solar cell achieving a power conversion efficiency of 15.45%, with a certified efficiency of 15.04%, according to pv magazine. Separately, a team at Wuhan University of Technology unveiled a polymer solar cell reaching 19.1% efficiency while retaining 97% of its performance after 2,000 hours of operation in air.

item.title: OpenAI raises record $110B from Amazon, Nvidia, SoftBank
item.description:
OpenAI announced on Friday a $110 billion funding round at a $730 billion pre-money valuation, the largest private financing deal ever recorded. The round includes $50 billion from Amazon, $30 billion from Nvidia, and $30 billion from SoftBank, with additional financial investors expected to join as the round progresses.

The deal cements a sweeping strategic partnership between OpenAI and Amazon and deepens the AI company's ties to its largest chip supplier, Nvidia, while more than doubling the $40 billion OpenAI raised in March 2025 in what was then the biggest private tech fundraise on record.

item.title: Green Party wins first-ever UK by-election, pushing Labour to third
item.description: Hannah Spencer, a 34-year-old plumber and local councillor, has won the Gorton and Denton by-election in Greater Manchester, delivering a result that marks the first time in the Green Party's history that it has won a UK parliamentary by-election. The victory, declared in the early hours of Friday morning, saw Spencer capture 14,980 votes — roughly 40.7% of the total — overturning a Labour majority of more than 13,000 from the 2024 general election. The result pushes Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party into third place in a seat the party had held for nearly a century.

item.title: IAEA says Iran stored near-weapons-grade uranium underground
item.description:
Some of Iran's most highly enriched uranium was stored in an underground tunnel complex at its nuclear site in Isfahan prior to last year's U.S. strikes, the International Atomic Energy Agency said in a confidential report circulated to member states on Friday, marking the first time the U.N. nuclear watchdog has specified where uranium enriched to up to 60% purity has been kept.

The disclosure adds a new dimension to the standoff over Tehran's nuclear program, arriving as the United States and Iran pursue fragile diplomatic negotiations and Washington maintains a large military buildup across the Middle East.

item.title: Trump warns of military force against Iran as nuclear talks stall
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday expressed frustration with the progress of nuclear negotiations with Iran and warned that military force remains on the table, telling reporters, "Don't want to, but sometimes you have to," when asked whether he would order strikes against the Islamic Republic.

Speaking to reporters before departing the White House for a trip to Texas, Trump said he was "not happy" with Iran's posture in the talks and reiterated his core demand. "I'm not happy with the fact that they're not willing to give us what we have to have. I'm not thrilled with that," he said, adding: "Iran cannot have nuclear weapons".

item.title: Taliban signal willingness to talk after Pakistan launches airstrikes
item.description:
Afghanistan's Taliban government said Friday it was open to negotiations with Pakistan, even as the two nations exchanged their most serious cross-border attacks in years. The diplomatic overture came hours after Pakistan launched airstrikes on Kabul, Kandahar, and Paktia province, with its defense minister declaring that the countries are now in a state of "open war."

The conflicting signals — a willingness to talk paired with escalating military operations — underscore the volatile and rapidly shifting dynamics between the once-allied neighbors, whose relationship has deteriorated sharply over Pakistan's accusations that the Taliban harbors militant groups responsible for attacks inside Pakistani territory.

item.title: Meloni calls Trump tariffs a 'mistake,' proposes EU-US free-trade zone
item.description:
In an interview with Bloomberg published Friday, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called for the European Union to form a free-trade zone with the United States, an ambitious proposal aimed at resolving the transatlantic tariff standoff that has rattled markets and stalled trade policy on both sides of the Atlantic.

Meloni described President Donald Trump's tariffs as a "mistake" and urged the EU to move forward with adopting the trade agreement it struck with Washington last summer, known as the Turnberry deal, according to Bloomberg. The deal, reached at Trump's Scottish golf resort in July 2025, set a 15% ceiling on tariffs for most EU exports to the United States in exchange for the EU eliminating import duties on all US industrial goods.

item.title: Fico says Ukraine has 'no interest' in restoring Druzhba oil pipeline after call with Zelenskyy
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico spoke by phone on Friday as a monthlong dispute over disrupted Russian oil supplies through the Druzhba pipeline showed no signs of resolution, with the standoff now blocking billions in EU financial aid to Kyiv and a new package of sanctions against Moscow.

Zelenskyy invited Fico to visit Ukraine to discuss "all issues" in person, according to a statement from the Ukrainian presidential office. Fico said he accepted the proposal for a meeting but would prefer it take place in an EU member state rather than in Ukraine. He offered a blunt assessment of the call: "I had the distinct impression that Ukraine has no interest in restoring oil transit through its territory."

item.title: Britain withdraws embassy staff from Iran amid US military buildup
item.description:
Britain withdrew its diplomatic staff from Iran and relocated embassy personnel inside Israel on Friday as a standoff with Washington over the use of the Diego Garcia military base deepened against a backdrop of faltering US-Iran nuclear negotiations and a massive American military buildup in the Middle East.

The White House is refusing to back the UK's agreement to hand sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius unless Prime Minister Keir Starmer allows the United States to use the jointly operated Diego Garcia base for potential strikes on Iran, according to Whitehall sources cited by GB News. Downing Street has so far resisted, with British officials arguing that permitting such an operation would violate international law.
